newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian power plant privatization on track.
newsitem.headline: Colombian power plant privatization on track.

text.p: The Colombian government rejected claims Monday that it had delayed the privatization of seven power generating plants and said it had received nine firm bids.
The spokesman in charge of the privatization process, Juan Fernando Bonilla, said the bids would be decided within the agreed time frame by Dec. 20.
"We haven't thought about delaying the process," he said.

The seven plants on the auction block, Termo Cartagena, Termo Tasajero, Betania, Chivor, Gualanday, Ocoa and Valle account for 20 percent of the national power output -- 10,000 megawatts. The total price was set at a minimum of $1.06 billion.
Bonilla said all nine bids were from potential foreign buyers in association with Colombian companies but declined to name any.

The Chilean companies Chilenger SA and Endesa have publicly expressed their interest in the process, particularly in Betania and Chivor. It is thought they will form consortia with Colombian and foreign firms.
